title: Local normalized branches in a finite coefficient-field tower
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $K\subseteq H\subseteq N$ be fields with $H/K$ and $N/H$ finite-dimensional. Put $E_H=(L\otimes_KH)_{\mathrm{red}}$, $E_N=(L\otimes_KN)_{\mathrm{red}}$, $R_H=\operatorname{IntCl}_A(H)$, $R_N=\operatorname{IntCl}_A(N)$, $C_H=\operatorname{IntCl}_B(E_H)$ and $C_N=\operatorname{IntCl}_B(E_N)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; reduction means quotient by all nilpotents. The natural maps $R_H\to R_N$ and $C_H\to C_N$ are injective and integral. Every maximal ideal of $C_H$ has a maximal ideal of $C_N$ above it. For a maximal ideal $q\subset C_H$, put $n=q\cap R_H$, $A_q=(R_H)_n$, $B_q=(C_H)_q$, and let $L_q$ be the fraction field of $B_q$. Then $n$ is maximal, $A_q,B_q$ are DVRs, and their fraction fields are $H,L_q$. The following are canonical identifications, compatible with all structural maps:
\[
 \operatorname{IntCl}_{A_q}(N)=(R_H\setminus n)^{-1}R_N,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{IntCl}_{B_q}((L_q\otimes_HN)_{\mathrm{red}})
       =(C_H\setminus q)^{-1}C_N.
\]
Here localization is [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], with the displayed multiplicative sets mapped to the respective rings. For every maximal $Q\subset C_N$ contracting to $q$, and $m=Q\cap R_N$, the local lower and upper DVRs obtained by these two successive normalizations are canonically $(R_N)_m$ and $(C_N)_Q$. No completeness, separability, module-finiteness of the integral closures, or perfectness of any residue field is assumed.

proof.text: The finite case of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], first for $P=H$ and then for $P=N$, applies to the given injective local DVR map. Here $N/K$ is finite: products of a $K$-basis of $H$ and an $H$-basis of $N$ span it. Thus $E_H,E_N$ are nonempty finite products of algebraic extensions of $L$; $R_H,R_N$ and $C_H,C_N$ have the stated normal domain factors. For every maximal $q$ of $C_H$ its contraction $n$ is maximal and $A_q,B_q$ are DVRs. Likewise every maximal $Q$ of $C_N$ contracts to a maximal $m$ of $R_N$ and gives DVRs $(R_N)_m,(C_N)_Q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], $R_H$ has fraction field $H$, and localization inside $H$ does not change that fraction field (every ratio of elements of $R_H$ remains a ratio of elements of $(R_H)_n$). Consequently $A_q$ has fraction field $H$.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction (1),(3); algebra.tex Tag 09IG, lemma-integral-closure-Dedekind; finite branch construction

proof.text: Put $T=L\otimes_KH$ and $U=L\otimes_KN$. Tensor universality identifies $T\otimes_HN$ with $U$, by $(l\otimes h)\otimes z\mapsto l\otimes hz$, with inverse $l\otimes z\mapsto(l\otimes1)\otimes z$. Apply [lem-sfb-field-extension-tensor-injective] over $H$ to the $H$-algebra $T$ and extension $N/H$ to see that $T\to U$ is injective. Its induced map $E_H\to E_N$ is injective: if the image of $t$ is nilpotent in $U$, injectivity gives $t^r=0$ in $T$ for the same exponent. Field inclusion similarly embeds $R_H$ into $R_N$. Images of integral elements remain integral, since applying a ring homomorphism to their monic equations preserves those equations. Hence the tensor map restricts to an injective map $C_H\to C_N$.

source.place: Tags 09EM, remark-construction, and 09ES, lemma-solutions-go-down, proof: iterated tensor identifications

proof.text: Every element of $R_N$ satisfies a monic equation over $A\subset R_H$, so $R_N$ is integral over $R_H$. Every element of $C_N$ satisfies one over $B\subset C_H$, so $C_N$ is integral over $C_H$. Moreover $\operatorname{IntCl}_{R_H}(N)=R_N$ and $\operatorname{IntCl}_{C_H}(E_N)=C_N$: the forward containments use [lem-sfb-integral-element-tower-descent] with the integral intermediate rings $R_H/A$ and $C_H/B$; the reverse containments reuse the original monic equations over $A$ or $B$. This does not assume that $E_N$ itself is integral over $C_H$.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction, tower construction; algebra.tex Tag 00GN, lemma-integral-transitive

proof.text: The injective integral map $C_H\to C_N$ has a prime above every prime of $C_H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over]. For a maximal $q$ choose such a prime $Q$ above it. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal], $Q$ is maximal, since its contraction is the maximal ideal $q$. This proves the asserted existence above every maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction (2),(3), applied to integral coefficient transition

proof.text: There is a canonical isomorphism $E_N\simeq(E_H\otimes_HN)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Indeed the map $T\to E_H$ induces $U=T\otimes_HN\to(E_H\otimes_HN)_{\mathrm{red}}$, which kills every nilpotent, and hence factors through $E_N$. Conversely $T\to E_N$ kills the nilradical of $T$, so factors through $E_H$; together with $N\to E_N$ this gives $E_H\otimes_HN\to E_N$, which factors through its reduction. The two composites are identities: both maps fix the images of $L$ and $N$, and these images generate both rings by tensor universality and quotient surjectivity. Thus no separability or assertion that the unreduced tensor is a product of fields is being used.

source.place: Tag 09ES, lemma-solutions-go-down, proof: equality of iterated reduced tensors; coefficient-tower version by tensor universal property

proof.text: Write $E_H=\prod_{i=1}^r F_i$ using step 1. Each $F_i/L$ is finite: it is a quotient of $L\otimes_KH$, which is spanned over $L$ by $1\otimes h_j$ for a finite $K$-basis $(h_j)$ of $H$. Put $D_i=\operatorname{IntCl}_B(F_i)$. Then $C_H=\prod_iD_i$: an integral tuple has integral coordinates; conversely, multiply a finite list of monic $B$-polynomials annihilating the coordinates to obtain one monic polynomial annihilating the tuple. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], $\operatorname{Frac}(D_i)=F_i$. The orthogonal idempotents $e_i$ belong to $C_H$ because $e_i^2-e_i=0$. Exactly one $e_i$ is outside $q$: at least one is outside since their sum is $1$, and at most one since $q$ is prime and $e_ie_j=0$ for $i\ne j$. Therefore $q$ is the inverse image of a prime $p\subset D_i$, and [lem-weil-pbc-product-prime-localization] identifies $B_q$ with $(D_i)_p$. Its fraction field $L_q$ is canonically $F_i$. For $S=C_H\setminus q$, the localization $S^{-1}E_H$ is also $F_i$: inverting $e_i$ kills all other factors, and every element of $S$ has nonzero $i$th coordinate, already a unit in $F_i$. Hence $S^{-1}E_H=L_q$ with its given $H$-map.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction (1),(3): componentwise normalization and local branches

proof.text: Set $V=R_H\setminus n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] to $R_H\to N$ and $V$, using $\operatorname{IntCl}_{R_H}(N)=R_N$ from step 3. Since $R_H\hookrightarrow H\hookrightarrow N$, every element of $V$ is nonzero in $N$ and thus already invertible. Accordingly $V^{-1}N=N$ and $V^{-1}R_H=A_q$. The lemma gives exactly $\operatorname{IntCl}_{A_q}(N)=V^{-1}R_N$, as subrings of $N$, with map $r/v\mapsto r/v$.

source.place: algebra.tex Tag 0307, lemma-integral-closure-localize, applied to the lower normalization

proof.text: For $S=C_H\setminus q$, step 5 induces $S^{-1}E_N\simeq(L_q\otimes_HN)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Here is an explicit universal-property check of the ambient identification. A map from $S^{-1}E_N$ to any reduced ring $Z$ is precisely a pair of compatible $H$-algebra maps $E_H\to Z$, $N\to Z$ such that the image of every $s\in S$ is a unit. Such a pair factors uniquely through $S^{-1}E_H=L_q$ and $N$, and hence through $(L_q\otimes_HN)_{\mathrm{red}}$. The localization of a reduced ring is reduced: if $(x/s)^d=0$, choose $t\in S$ with $tx^d=0$; then $(tx)^d=0$, so $tx=0$ and $x/s=0$. Both source rings are therefore reduced, and the preceding factorization constructs inverse maps by taking $Z$ equal to either source. On the generators their formula is $[\bar t\otimes z]/s\mapsto(\bar t/s)\otimes z$. This also proves compatibility with the $B_q$-structure.

source.place: Tag 09ES, lemma-solutions-go-down, proof, reduced tensor identification after selecting a local branch; elementary fraction universal property

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] now to $C_H\to E_N$ and $S=C_H\setminus q$. Step 3 identifies its unlocalized integral closure with $C_N$, whereas $S^{-1}C_H=B_q$ and step 8 identifies $S^{-1}E_N$ with $(L_q\otimes_HN)_{\mathrm{red}}$. The resulting equality of subrings is $\operatorname{IntCl}_{B_q}((L_q\otimes_HN)_{\mathrm{red}})=S^{-1}C_N$. In particular localization removes the other generic factors; one does not assume that $E_H$ is a field before localization.

source.place: algebra.tex Tag 0307, lemma-integral-closure-localize, applied to the upper normalization

proof.text: Fix a maximal $Q\subset C_N$ above $q$ and put $m=Q\cap R_N$. Step 1 gives maximality of $m$ and the direct-normalization DVRs. Commutativity of the inclusions gives $m\cap R_H=n$, so $V$ misses $m$ and $S$ misses $Q$. The corresponding ideals of $V^{-1}R_N$ and $S^{-1}C_N$ are $V^{-1}m$ and $S^{-1}Q$; they are maximal because their quotient rings are the fields $R_N/m$ and $C_N/Q$ (all inverted denominators have nonzero images). Localizing at these ideals gives $(R_N)_m$ and $(C_N)_Q$. Explicitly $(r/v)/(t/w)\mapsto rw/(vt)$, where $t\notin m$ (respectively $Q$), is inverse to $r/t\mapsto(r/1)/(t/1)$. These inverse fraction maps preserve lower-to-upper inclusions since both send a numerator and denominator to their images. The two successive normalizations in steps 7 and 9 therefore give exactly the direct local DVRs.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction (3); algebra.tex Tag 0307, lemma-integral-closure-localize, followed by elementary localization of fractions

proof.text: All identifications used above are induced by the original inclusions, the pure-tensor map $(l\otimes h)\otimes z\mapsto l\otimes hz$, reduction quotient maps, and the fraction maps $x/s\mapsto x/s$. Their composites agree on the original ring elements, pure tensors and inverse denominators, which generate the respective rings. Thus they commute with every structural map in the asserted coefficient tower and with the passage to the indicated local branches. The argument used only finite-dimensionality of $H/K$ and $N/H$; no step required completeness, separability, finite generation of an integral closure as a module, or a perfect residue field.
